mainEntity.name: Why do I crash every afternoon after lunch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frequent drivers include large high-carb lunches, blood sugar peaks and drops, insulin resistance, poor sleep, and stress. Daily severe crashes deserve medical review.

mainEntity.name: Why am I so tired after lunch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild post-lunch sleepiness can be normal. Disabling fatigue suggests meal composition, metabolic, or sleep disorders worth evaluating.

mainEntity.name: What is an afternoon energy crash?

acceptedAnswer.text: A predictable slump in alertness and mood 1–3 hours after midday eating, often with brain fog and carb cravings.

mainEntity.name: Is afternoon fatigue a sign of diabetes?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can occur with prediabetes or diabetes but is not specific. Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, or elevated A1C increase concern.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop post-lunch sleepiness at work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smaller protein-forward lunches, post-meal walks, hydration, sleep optimization, and clinician-guided metabolic testing when persistent.

mainEntity.name: Afternoon crash vs brain fog after eating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Overlapping topics. This guide centers afternoon timing; see brain fog after eating for wider differential and insulin resistance detail.
